name: ETH dip + consolidation + pullback · trend exit

consolidation_breakout.description: A second way in, for when ETH never comes back down to its average: buy the break out of a quiet band.
consolidation_breakout.condition: The 12 bars before the current one sit inside a band no wider than 2.5% (highest high / lowest low - 1). The first bar to close above that band's top is the break; 30 minutes later the 1-minute close must still be above the top, and the buy lands on the next minute's open. Only the first break of each quiet stretch counts.
consolidation_breakout.market_filter: Only the blocked hours are shared with the dip rule. The downtrend filter is deliberately NOT applied: requiring the averages to be stacked upward before a break screens out exactly the breaks that start a new trend, and it lost money on both ETH and SOL in the backtest.

exit.note: A break comes out of a tighter band than a dip buys into, so it carries its own stop and trail. The trend ride applies to these lots on the same terms as any other.

pullback_to_trend.description: A third way in, for when ETH trends upward in a wide range: it never comes back to its 7-day average and never goes quiet enough for the quiet-band breakout. Buy the end of a short pullback inside the uptrend.
pullback_to_trend.condition: The daily averages for that UTC day are stacked 7d > 15d > 30d. A run of at least 180 consecutive 1-minute closes below the 1440-minute EMA of 1-minute closes (pandas ewm span=1440, adjust=False) ends with the first close back above it; the buy lands on the next minute's open. Only the blocked hours are shared with the dip rule.
pullback_to_trend.lots: Shares the coin's lots with the dip and the quiet-band breakout, first come first served. Separate pullback lots were built and then removed: they only pay once the core is full (5 lots), and below that the reserved slots sit idle while the dip waits.
pullback_to_trend.exit: The dip's exit: stop -4.5%, trail arms at +1.315%, and because it only buys in an uptrend it is a trend-ride lot held against the 16-hour EMA.

entry.pyramid_add_removed: ETH had a pyramid add-on: while a lot was winning, another lot was added at +1% steps above its fill, up to three. It is removed, not switched off. Measured over Oct 2024 - Jul 2026 on 5 shared lots it added +14.6% of the money across 172 adds at a 54.1% win rate, while dropping the whole strategy's win rate from 85.4% to 76.6% and deepening the worst mark-to-market dip from -9.66% to -14.06% - and it took 28 lots the dip would otherwise have used. Not worth the money or the noise. SOL keeps its own add-on, which is a different rule (+0.5% steps, sold with its parent).

break_even_floor.description: The break-even floor. The moment a lot arms - reaches the trail activation - a lot that is being held against the trend line has its protective stop lifted from the -X% level to its own buy price plus the cost of a round trip, and the order parked on Binance is cancelled and re-placed at the new level. A lot that has proved itself and then comes all the way back exits level instead of slightly negative.
break_even_floor.break_even_floor_pct: Derived, never hard-coded: (bnb_fee_bps_per_side + slippage_bps_per_side) * 2 / 100 from this file's execution_model. At 7.5bps fee and 2bps slippage that is 0.19%.
break_even_floor.applies_to: Trend-ride lots only - the ones opened in a clean uptrend and held against the line. Trailing-stop lots keep the giveback trail and never get a floor.
break_even_floor.requires_arming: Yes. A lot that never reaches the trail activation keeps only its protective stop. Attaching the floor earlier - as soon as a lot has merely traded above its costs - was tested and is far worse: it turns a normal wobble on the way up into an exit (walk-forward +33.8% against +82.0% of the money, better in 0 of 6 windows).
break_even_floor.never_caps_a_winner: A lot that trends does not return to its own buy price, so the floor is simply never reached and the line takes the lot out far above it.
break_even_floor.evidence: ETH, 5 shared lots, Oct 2024 - Jul 2026: losing lots 105 -> 67, win rate 77.1% -> 85.4%, profit +83.1% -> +86.0% of the money, better in 6 of 6 walk-forward windows. The two variants people reach for first were both rejected: a floor that rides 0.19% above the trend line instead of sitting at the buy price (walk-forward +65.0% against +82.0% - it is a moving level, so it sells the dips that trending lots recover from), and dropping the arming requirement. See research/backtests/scripts/eth_line_gap.py and eth_floor_and_arm.py.

trend_exit.condition: Once the trail has armed, a lot opened while 7d > 15d > 30d ignores the giveback and is sold at the next minute's open after a 1-minute close below the 960-minute EMA of 1-minute closes (pandas ewm span=960, adjust=False). The protective stop stays active throughout. From the minute after it arms the protective stop sits at the break-even floor, not the original level, so the lot cannot finish negative while it waits for the line.
trend_exit.fallback: Lots opened outside a clean uptrend keep the giveback trailing stop below.

portfolio.sizing_rule: Every coin that is switched on shares one pot of equal lots, set in the dashboard. A trade buys one full lot when a lot is free and the wallet has the USDT for it; when less than a full lot is left, the buy uses what is left. Money is never set per coin.

provenance.research: Scripts in research/backtests/scripts: eth_ema_exit_grid.py (trend-ride grid), run_eth_consolidation_full.py (quiet-band breakout), eth_three_modes.py, eth_pullback.py, eth_sleeves.py, eth_core_lots.py, eth_sleeves_core5.py; parity with the engine: verify_pullback_parity.py. Summary: research/backtests/results/eth_consolidation_families.csv. The large raw grids are regenerated by the scripts, not stored.
provenance.backtest_bnb_fees: Oct 2024 - Aug 2026, BNB fees, one shared wallet; percentages are of the money in the lots. Core only (dip + quiet-band breakout): 1 lot +107.5%, 3 lots +93.5%, 5 lots +82.5%, all 6/6 walk-forward windows. With the pullback sharing the same lots: 1 lot +74.2%, 3 lots +88.5%, 5 lots +82.8% (walk-forward +78.8% against +75.7%). The pullback pays for its slot only once the core is full; below that it costs the dip trades it displaces. Pyramid adds (+1% steps, up to 3) with 3 lots of their own on top of core 5 + pullback 2 earned more in total but less per lot, 243 adds at a 58.4% win rate; it has since been removed.
provenance.caveats: The pullback's measured gain (about +18% of a 5-lot core's money, honest) was earned with lots RESERVED for it; sharing lots is worse at small sizes, so on a small account the pullback is close to free optionality and at 1 lot it cost about a third of that lot over 22 months. Its edge is also lumpy: 83% of that gain came from one strong uptrend (April 2025). The 24h / 180-minute setting was chosen on this same history. The pyramid's honest figure was much smaller than its backtest: choosing its rule in advance gave +41% of its 3 lots' money (4/6 windows), and almost all of that came from one window (April 2025). It was worth its lots only once the core was at 5 and the pullback near 4 - about ten lots in ETH.
